s.n: Cat lady cover croque monsieur bites
s.note: Susan's first cover, the frumpy cat lady
s.how: Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 200ml milk and simmer until thick. Season with nutmeg and stir in 40g grated gruyère. Spread 8 slices of white bread thinly with Dijon mustard. Make 4 sandwiches with 150g sliced leg ham and 80g gruyère. Fry in butter for 2 minutes a side, then spread the béchamel on top, scatter with 40g more gruyère and grill 3 minutes until bubbling. Cut into fingers.

s.n: Budapest garlic lángos with sour cream
s.note: the Budapest leg of the mission
s.how: Divide 500g pizza dough into 4 balls and rest 15 minutes. Stretch each by hand into a 15cm round, thinner in the middle. Fry in 3cm of oil at 180C for 90 seconds a side until puffed and golden, then drain. Mix 2 crushed garlic cloves with 3 tbsp olive oil and brush over the hot bread. Spread each with 3 tbsp sour cream, scatter with 120g grated tasty cheese and finish with sweet paprika and chopped dill.

m.n: Rome cacio e pepe with toasted pepper
m.how: Cook 400g spaghetti in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Meanwhile toast 2 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper in a large dry frying pan for 1 minute, then add 30g butter and a ladle of the pasta water. Finely grate 150g pecorino and mix to a paste with 4 tbsp cool pasta water. Move the pasta into the pepper pan with a splash more water and toss 1 minute. Off the heat, toss in the cheese paste until glossy and serve with extra pecorino.

w.how: Mix 300g self-raising flour, 300g caster sugar, 60g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Whisk in 2 eggs, 250ml milk, 125ml vegetable oil and 250ml hot coffee to a thin batter. Pour into a lined 23 x 33cm tin and bake at 180C for 30 minutes. Cool. For the icing, melt 100g butter and 150g dark chocolate, then beat in 250g icing sugar and 3 tbsp milk. Spread over the cake and scatter with 60g chopped toasted hazelnuts.

d.note: Rayna and her very big hair in Rome
d.how: Fill 4 large wine glasses with ice. Pour 60ml bitter orange aperitif into each, then add 90ml chilled prosecco and 30ml soda water. Stir gently once. Slide a thick wedge of blood orange, or regular orange, into each glass and serve with a small bowl of green olives on the side. For anyone not drinking, mix blood orange juice with soda and a dash of bitters.
